title: Canva Cuts 1,271 Jobs as AI Costs and Chatbots Squeeze a Decade of Growth
excerpt: The design platform's first growth slowdown in ten years has triggered its first mass restructuring — a case study in how AI raises costs for the companies it also competes with.
body:
• Canva is cutting 22% of its staff — 1,271 people — in a restructuring that also merges its product, growth and platform teams; some affected staff will be reassigned or relocated rather than laid off.
  • CEO Melanie Perkins told staff growth has slowed for the first time in a decade, in what she called the company's hardest year yet.
  • Canva cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20% in August because the cost of serving AI features ran too high; early investors marked its valuation down to about $35 billion.
  • The squeeze is two-sided: AI is expensive for Canva to run, while ChatGPT and Gemini now make posters and presentations free for casual users.

Canva, the Australian design platform used by hundreds of millions of people to make posters, slides and social posts, is cutting 22% of its staff — 1,271 people — after its growth slowed for the first time in a decade. Co-founder and CEO Melanie Perkins announced the restructuring in a note to employees, reported by TechCrunch, calling this the company's hardest year yet and saying small changes would not be enough.

"This has been our hardest year yet, and as we shared earlier this year, our growth has slowed for the first time in a decade."

— Melanie Perkins, co-founder and CEO, Canva

What is changing inside Canva

The company is merging its product, growth and platform teams into one organisation to reduce communication friction, cutting back on narrow subspecialisation so employees take on broader responsibilities, and moving toward hybrid work with more product work centralised in Sydney. Reporting by Fast Company notes that the 1,271 figure covers people who will be laid off, reassigned to new roles, or relocated — Canva has not broken down how many fall into each group. A company-wide meeting is scheduled for November 10.

The cost side: AI is not free to serve

Software used to cost almost nothing to serve to one more user. AI features break that model: every generated image costs real computing money. Canva has been shipping its own AI models to reduce costs and reliance on third-party providers, but in August it still cut its 2026 revenue growth forecast from 30% to 20%, telling investors the average cost of serving an AI task was too high. Perkins has since said the cost per AI task has fallen sharply as the company reworked its approach — but the forecast cut stood, and early investors marked Canva's valuation down to about $35 billion, from $42 billion.

The competition side: the chatbot does design now

At the same time, general-purpose chatbots have learned Canva's core trick. ChatGPT and Gemini can now generate posters, social graphics and presentation slides directly from a text prompt, and casual users increasingly skip a dedicated design app altogether. That is the double squeeze The Hindu's explainer on the layoffs sets out: AI raises Canva's own costs while handing its most casual customers a free alternative.

What to watch

Canva remains large by any measure — it reported more than 265 million monthly active users and more than 31 million paid users by the end of 2025, and second-quarter revenue of $921.9 million, up 25.2% year on year. The question the restructuring has to answer is whether a design platform built for the pre-AI era can keep its paying professionals while chatbots absorb the casual end of the market — and whether its own AI features can be served cheaply enough to defend both ends at once.
nri_angle: Canva is a daily tool for many diaspora creators and small businesses; its AI cost squeeze mirrors what Indian SaaS and design teams are facing on serving costs.
author: Diaspora Desk
